title: A substantial extremal theorem from exponent lattice orderings
objective: Achieve a substantial mathematical advance connected to the smooth-number exponent-lattice observations, with resolving a recognized quantitative problem as the success criterion rather than producing another manuscript. The concrete first target is the worst-case number G_3(n) of distinct monomial initial ideals of a length-n polynomial quotient in three variables, over all fields. Determine its sharp asymptotic growth, or prove an infinite realizable family with a polynomially larger number of orderings than the generic corner-cut scale, together with a consequential general theorem. Explain what algebraic dependencies add to the prime/smooth lattice geometry. First audit the strongest relevant primary literature and the repository's unfinished lattice-shadow work; distinguish a genuinely new theorem from a classical geometric corollary before using it. Success requires a complete uniform proof that settles this extremal question or a substantial recognized part of it, a rigorous consequence for algebraic or geometric complexity beyond restating the count, independently implemented reproducible supporting checks, and an honestly attributed paper. A draft, a bounded priority review, isolated examples, a minor refinement, or an unverified novelty claim cannot complete this goal. If this target is already settled or a route fails, record the evidence and choose a comparably consequential problem still directly linked to the original mathematics; do not silently lower the success criterion. Preserve all existing manuscripts, core smooth-number kernels and auditor, previous research, and the paused ML work. Never send emails, messages to people or other tasks, author queries, or submissions. Publish only explicitly privacy-reviewed research files to the already authorized main branch.
note: Completed low layers now confine the changing tower problem to a fixed contracted column space and give a uniform regional count O(n^(3/2)*sqrt(D)*K), including a wider quadratic region. A separate classical periodic-carrier corollary bounds every positive price by O(n^(7/3)) for comparable coprime periods. These are family upper bounds; neither proves sharp G3 growth, a polynomially separating actual lower family, novelty or publication significance. The original goal remains active.
relationship_to_previous_work: New active objective with a higher completion bar. Previous goal records, lattice-shadow candidate, manuscripts and paused ML results are preserved as historical research.

definitions.G_d_n: Maximum number of monomial initial ideals of a colength-n ideal in d variables, over all fields.
definitions.F_d_n: The corresponding maximum for n distinct rational points; F_d(n) <= G_d(n).

success_criteria: Sharp asymptotic growth for G_3(n), or an infinite realizable family polynomially above the generic corner-cut scale together with a consequential general theorem.
A complete uniform proof settling the target or a substantial recognized part, and a further rigorous algebraic or geometric consequence beyond restating the count.
A current primary-source comparison establishing the exact novelty boundary; an unavailable paper does not establish novelty.
Independent reproducible supporting checks and an honestly attributed paper; acceptance and impact are not presumed.
A draft, isolated examples, a bounded search, a minor refinement or an unverified novelty claim cannot complete the goal.

A cyclic assignment of each fixed-(x,y) monomial group to distinct planes gives a nonzero product of ordinary Vandermonde determinants as one coefficient of its evaluation determinant. For positive cuts relative to any anchored axis box, included axis counts satisfy n<=product(lengths)<=d^d*n. Every pair is feasible by an explicit interval for the z cost. The known planar Theta(n*log(n)) count gives Theta(n^2*log(n)) for two layers. uniform_proofs: Let a rank-r matroid have the entire ground {a in N_0^d:m.a<L} and allow replacing any selected element by any unselected element of no larger additive valuation. At a tied feasible exchange e to f at positive cost t, every unselected element with valuation at most max(v(e),v(f)) is also a feasible replacement for e. Optimality puts all points strictly cheaper than t in that valuation prefix into the basis. There are at most r-1 of them.

The closed cheap prefix is an intersection of two positive halfspaces in the orthant. Floor-halving maps it to the strict prefix with fibers at most 2^d; an explicit 1/d inner grid bounds its box by d^d times its size. Thus every raw tied feasible exchange satisfies product_i(|f_i-e_i|+1)<=(2*d)^d*(r-1), uniformly in the ground size, truncation and valuation vector. The primitive direction satisfies the same bound.

Classical matroid exchange geometry makes every positive cone facet one of those directions. A single hyperbolic cross has O_d(r*log(r+1)^(d-1)) possible normals; the classical central arrangement gives O_d(r^(d-1)*log(r+1)^((d-1)^2)) positive bases. A shared list of positive integer weights of that size samples all such rank-r matroids, with coordinate heights O_d(r^(d-1)) by cofactors. Shared-list sampling and the Hilbert-zonotope method are prior art; the extra content is the rank-sized direction estimate under the lowering hypothesis.

Every explicit quotient I_(L,m) from the ordered exponential construction satisfies the lowering property, in every fixed dimension. Its actual length is n=L-max_k(k-nu_m(k)). The entire characteristic-zero family, including unequal valuations and embedding dimension three, therefore has the generic polynomial exponent d-1 up to logarithmic factors. In three variables its count is O(n^2*log(n+1)^4). This closes the whole construction as a power-separation route.

For normalized truncated power series with any fixed leading orders m, the same dimension obstruction bounds ranks for all coefficients. Each subset meeting the rank inequalities has a minor nonzero at the explicit exponential point. A finite product of these minors proves a nonempty Zariski-open coefficient locus with exactly the same nested rank rule and actual length. Thus generic one-parameter Taylor jets also cannot give a polynomial separation. Specialization can add dependencies and can change the quotient length.

The all-field binomial algebra (z,xy,x^(p+1),y^(q+1),x^p-y^q), with coprime p,q, has length p+q and exactly two initial ideals. Its primitive wall normal (p,-q,0) has product (p+1)*(q+1), quadratic in length for consecutive p,q. No full positive additive valuation order containing the nonzero socle representatives satisfies the lowering property, because one representative has valuation at least that of the zero monomial xy. For rank-two profile lattice L, use a lattice basis as projection rows. Cauchy--Binet gives c=sum(p_ij^2), hence eta=sum(abs(p_ij))/sum(p_ij^2)<=1. Nonprimitive independent row choices give the same ratio if the actual image lattice is used. Projection preserves every vertex of the profile plane.

The complement algebra C=B/((U-1)*(V-1)*(W-1)) has length M-n. Its inverse-monomial columns represent the known dual matroid, via the perfect coefficient-of-one pairing. It has a fixed degree-six carrier in X,Y,Z. Actual omissions maximize costs on inverse labels in the finite cover standard set. Reflection makes these finite-ground minimum costs, but for a nonbox cover ground the reflected ground lacks the constant monomial and cannot contain a global standard set of C. An exact positively coherent (5,7,11) basis at the stated near-total-degree weight has integral index two, rank 239 modulo two, and changes XY^11 to Y^12 in characteristic two. All strict borders, ordinary degree distributions and integer determinants are independently checked. Two divides none of the periods, so repeated roots are not needed. Every finite monomial self-map of affine three-space sending variables to nonconstant monomials is a permutation of pure-power maps: each coordinate axis requires a pure-power image for the origin fiber to be finite. Every top-cell point has an upper interval of size at most H=2^L, so the H-shell contains more than half the downset. The shell bound therefore controls how many basis monomials can have multiplication rank at most k over every field. Its top X layer has T=L^2*binomial(R+1,2) points, each with upper interval at most k=L^2 and each surviving the oriented cube test because its +2e_X corner is absent. uniform_proofs: For spanning subgraphs on the same vertices, the cycle-space intersection is the cycle space of their intersection. The loss from replacing their cycle sum by union cycles is c(intersection)-c(H)-c(Hprime)+c(union), over every field. Zero loss permits an exact merge of integer cycle lattices as well. Dropping acyclic groups and making such merges preserves the sum. At most two surviving cyclic groups have graph-only rank. A failed greedy merge order does not prove that every merge order fails.

Choose a base graph and extend one of its spanning forests to the union. Fundamental cycles have integral chord coordinates. The base cycle space supplies unit coordinates, and projection to the other chords gives a zero/plus/minus-one residual matrix R. The full cycle-sum rank is z(base)+rank_K(R), in every characteristic. Combined with the existing tensor/cographic identity this gives the exact prefix rank. The published coefficient-deletion formula replaces T^119 by T^240 with index three, because coefficient 119 is -3. Its 21-by-21 residual matrix has twenty unit pivots and remainder [3]. uniform_proofs: For any three-dimensional polytope, the number of vertices incident to edges parallel to a fixed nonzero q is at most twice the number of vertices of its projection along q. Each exposed vertex fiber is a point or a segment. This includes endpoints of collapsed edges, which need not be strictly visible individually. The statement covers lower-dimensional polytopes as well and is elementary classical projection geometry.

For rho(q)=product_i(|q_i|+1), the sum of 1+||q||_1^(1/3) over nonzero primitive integer directions up to sign with rho(q)<=T is O(T^(4/3)), without additional logarithms in T. Overcounting all signs and setting u_i=|q_i|+1 reduces this to sum_(u1*u2*u3<=T) u1^(1/3)<=16*T^(4/3), by the convergent exponent-4/3 sums. Combining this with the existing all-field rational-shadow theorem proves L_T(I)=O(n*T^(4/3)*log(n+1)) for all positive initial cells incident to an interior wall below that product threshold.

For labels in one dyadic box of product at most 8n, a nonzero difference has primitive product at most 8n. Thus any actual within-box optimal matroid wall exchange contributes only O(n^(7/3)*log(n+1)) incident states overall. This does not assert a within-box exchange for every wall or one for every cone. After the previous boundary cover, g(I)<=O(n^(5/3)*log(n+1)+n*T^(4/3)*log(n+1))+R_T(I), where R_T counts nonboundary cells with no incident product-small wall. That remainder has not been bounded above.

Classical planar support enumeration plus two fiber endpoint support calls per projected vertex gives O(n*T^(4/3)*log(n+1)) greedy calls to a superset of the specified initial states. If w is a positive integer exposing objective and the profile coordinate widths are at most R, epsilon=1/(2*(R+1)*||q||_1+1) keeps w plus/minus epsilon*q positive, preserves the exposed fiber and selects its endpoints. This is a theoretical support-oracle reduction, not a newly implemented enumeration algorithm or a field-operation bound. The previous border-generator count gives O(n^(5/3)*T^(4/3)*log(n+1)) reduced-basis polynomials for this part of the fan.

In the known three-pole quotient, a positive allocation a1+a2+a3=n-1 has six actual facet directions prim((ai+1)*ei-aj*ej), i!=j. Choose a1,a2 in [ceil(n/4),floor(3n/8)] for n>=16; there are at least n^2/256 choices and each ai lies between n/8 and n/2. For each of the six pairs, at most n^2/G allocations have gcd(ai+1,aj)>G, since the pair map is injective into positive integers at most n and sum_(d>G) floor(n/d)^2<=n^2/G. With G=4096, at least 5*n^2/2048 entirely interior cells have every primitive wall product at least n^2/(64*G^2). Consequently R_T is Omega(n^2) for T below that quadratic threshold, while the whole known fan remains exactly binomial(n+1,2). continuations.progress_classification: A proposed grouping mechanism for the remainder R_T is now assessed exactly. Two internally fixed cost lists reduce to a partial matching; Gusfield (1984) is direct prior art for this setting, with no new-theorem priority claim. Three lists admit a signed prefix-rank formula with at most 2*r^2 interior terms, compiled using O(|E|+r^2*log(r+1)) rank calls and queried in O(r^2) arithmetic/comparison operations without more rank calls. Uniform prefix rank already has r^2 signed corrections. uniform_proofs: In any internally fixed list, an element dependent on earlier elements of the same list can be discarded for every respecting greedy order. Each list compresses to at most rank r elements. For two compressed lists, the mixed second rank differences are the indicators of parallel nonloops after contracting the two earlier prefixes. They are nonnegative zero/one entries and telescope to row and column sums at most one: a partial matching of size p+q-r. The minimum basis cost is the sum of unmatched costs plus the minimum cost of each matched pair, on the fixed internal-order domain. For linear three-parameter costs this gives a local arrangement of at most r lines and a quadratic local cell bound. The setting has explicit old prior art and is not treated as a new generic matroid theorem.

For three compressed lists, finite prefix-grid Mobius inversion writes the greedy basis cost as single costs minus boundary pair maxima plus signed triple maxima. For fixed first/second indices, the pair is parallel after contracting the third prefix on at most one interval: pair rank gain is nonincreasing, and once either element is a loop it stays a loop. The interior mixed third rank differences are the two signed interval endpoints, at most two per first/second pair and at most 2*r^2 in all. Three monotone gain thresholds locate the interval by binary search. Preprocessing uses O(|E|+r^2*log(r+1)) rank-oracle calls; each generic query evaluates O(r^2) signed maxima and recovers an actual zero/one basis indicator without new rank calls. These are oracle bounds, not field-operation or bit-complexity claims, and exact current priority is unassessed.

The rank-two lists (e1),(e2),(e1+e2,e1) have pair-parallelism sequence zero,one,zero along the third prefix, so both signs are necessary in this expansion. For the uniform prefix model R(i,j,k)=min(r,i+j+k), the mixed third coefficients are minus one at i+j+k=r+1 and plus one at i+j+k=r+2, with exactly r^2 nonzero terms. This proves quadratic order for this prefix-grid coefficient count, not a lower bound for every optimization representation or a fan-count lower bound.

For the known actual three-pole quotient, after contracting the constant the rank of every three-axis prefix union is min(n-1,i+j+k). Ordinary quotient arithmetic independently checks the model in four fields. This does not identify the full residue matroid with a uniform matroid. Every positive standard set is the constant plus the n-1 cheapest axis points. In any domain preserving two internal total orders on any partition of those points, the first n-1 points are determined by their occupancy in one list, giving at most n possible standard sets. The previously proved 5*n^2/2048 large-wall interior cells therefore require at least 5*n/2048 such domains. A universal polylogarithmic two-list-domain cover is impossible, while aggregate overlap accounting, smaller local estimates or other structural methods remain possible.

uniform_proofs: Over Z[s,p], explicit ideal identities and six S-pair certificates prove that (XZ-Z-1,X^2Y^2-sXY+p) has bases (g1,g3,g4) when w_X>w_Z and (g1,g2,g3) when w_Z>w_X. Every reduction head is below its least-common-multiple throughout the whole stated cone, so no parameter specialization or characteristic restriction is hidden. The curve standard monomials lie on six explicitly specified rays in each domain.

For component functional ranks d1,d2 and union rank d, generic evaluation at m1,m2 nodes has rank min(m1+m2,m2+d1,m1+d2,d), by the established Rado independent-representatives max-min formula and multilinearity of evaluation minors. On actual monomial cost prefixes, both component functional ranks equal the primary-axis count k, and union rank equals k+q. Thus generic prefix rank is min(n,k+min(L,q)), L=min(m1,m2). The same nonempty open node condition works simultaneously for every possible selected basis. This is a prefix statement, not identification of the complete residue matroid with a quota matroid.

Before the secondary quota saturates, the basis is a strict size-n cut on six rays. Normalize w_Y=1 and fix j=floor(h). For Q points on the paired Z rays there are O(1+j/Q^2) possible secondary-Y occupancies; each determines P on the paired X rays. At fixed P,Q the two primary counts are monotone functions of the same threshold h, with O(1+n/j^2) possible pairs. Summing over j,Q gives O(n^2) for every positive aspect ratio. This uses a shared threshold and does not multiply separate allocation counts.

After saturation, the basis consists of the first H=max(m1,m2) primary and first L secondary points. Three-axis counts at rank r approximate r times normalized reciprocal prices to absolute error below three. Since L<=H-1 in this regime, the first L axis allocation is determined to bounded error by the H-1 nonconstant primary allocation. Secondary costs shift only the Y arm by the cheaper X/Z price, changing the other two counts by at most one each. This gives only a constant number of secondary allocations per primary allocation, hence O(n^2) uniformly in the component sizes.

There are Omega(H^2) primary allocations with all weights within ratio two. At such weights the secondary rays lag their primary images by at most four minimum-price units. An unsaturated size-n cut has at most eight primary selections beyond H; a saturated selection has exactly H. Each final selected set therefore represents only constantly many original H-primary allocations, proving Omega(n^2). The result covers all characteristics over suitable infinite fields and does not assert rational generic witnesses over every fixed finite field.

Distinct node values alone do not ensure genericity: alpha=(1,2), nodes (2,3) and (4,5), give rank three for (1,Y,Y^2,Y^3), because two distinct spatial points share Y=1/2. Special samples and variable numbers of components remain unresolved and cannot be excluded by the generic theorem.

uniform_proofs: For monic f of degree s, define H_h as the ordinary normal form of Z^h*f(XY) modulo g=XZ-Z-1. Its leading term is Y^s times the larger of X^(s-h), Z^h. If ell=floor(s*w_X/(w_X+w_Z)), the basis (g,H_ell,H_(ell+1)) has heads XZ, X^(s-ell)*Y^s, Y^s*Z^(ell+1). The identities Z*H_h=H_(h+1) and X*H_(h+1)=H_h+H_(h+1) modulo g give two standard S-pair representations with heads strictly below their least common multiples throughout the sector. The classical chain criterion gives the third pair. Since Z is a unit modulo g, these polynomials generate the carrier ideal. This is a uniform proof for every degree and characteristic, not an extrapolation of the formal fixtures.

Merge the pure X/Z axis monomials as t_i with costs v_i. The first s axis monomials are exactly the axis footprint between the two carrier heads, and all carrier-standard monomials are t_i*Y^b with min(i,b)<s. Thus every s-component subset has the same cost-prefix functional rank d_s, independent of which distinct nonzero component scalars it contains. Generic sampling at component sizes m_j has weighted affine Hilbert function min_s(n-A_s+d_s), where A_s is the sum of the s largest component sizes. This is the established independent-representatives formula applied to the actual functional prefix ranks, not a claim that arbitrary residue subsets have a uniform or capacity matroid.

A single nonempty open node condition gives all weighted Hilbert functions and the positive fan simultaneously: every partial positive greedy selection is a downset of size at most n and lies in the finite universal hyperbolic ground. Every full prefix evaluation rank equals its intersection rank with that ground for every point configuration of the stated length. Impose generic Rado ranks on its finitely many subsets. This avoids an infinite intersection. Component-subset symmetry makes d_s concave by row-space submodularity. For equal component sizes, the Rado minimum is at an endpoint, giving exact truncation min(n,d_r).

An excluded hook point has both indices at least s and has s^2 strictly cheaper allowed points. Therefore all first-N prefixes agree with the enclosing-surface prefixes if N<=s^2, and all capacity constraints with s^2>=n are redundant. The exact general rank needs only q=min(r,floor(sqrt(n-1))) largest component sizes, total n, and the enclosing-surface count. For balanced samples r^2>=n this proves equality of the full finite fan with the generic surface fan, without assuming that curve-generic nodes are surface-generic.

Each of the r balanced carrier sectors is uniform n-subset selection from an orthant-boundary ground of O(n*log(n+1)) points. The established convex-position strict-set bound yields O(r*n^2*log(n+1)) states; for r^2>=n, surface equality gives O(n^2*log(n+1)). Together these give the uniform restricted O(n^(5/2)*log(n+1)) upper bound. A fixed polynomial gain in this balanced family would require a polynomially increasing r<sqrt(n). The intermediate range and the general unequal-size count remain unresolved.

The hook rank increment is the sum of one row count and one column count. Generating the first q costs v_i takes a two-axis merge; all required d_s take O(q) arithmetic/comparison operations. The enclosing-surface rank is the sum of two planar lattice counts minus their shared axis, evaluable by established Euclidean floor sums in O(log W) arithmetic steps for integer prices and threshold. After O(r*log(q+2)) standard size-selection preprocessing and O(q+1) retained data, a promised-generic weighted-Hilbert-function query costs O(q+log W), with no evaluation matrices. uniform_proofs: Let J subset I contain XZ-Z-1, let I have length n, and assume every positive monomial prefix has rank in I equal to min(n, its carrier rank in J). If primitive integer planes with normals q cover all internal carrier walls, then g(I)=O(n*log(n+1)*(n+sum_q ||q||_1^(1/3))). This is a conditional structural reduction, not a count for all quotients on the surface. All carrier-standard monomials lie on the XY/YZ exponent planes; off carrier walls finite selection is the n cheapest such monomials.

An off-carrier interior fan vertex has noncollinear threshold points, hence at least two on one exponent plane and a threshold point with positive transverse exponent. Fix an XY tie direction and cost. Its strictly cheaper planar carrier space has rank k<n and its full planar tie has gain G>=2. As the Z price increases, both strict and closed full-prefix carrier ranks are nonincreasing, so the interval where the threshold can affect rank n is connected. Away from transverse ties, strict rank has at most g0=min(G,n-k) values. Each off-carrier vertex strictly decreases that rank; accounting for interval endpoints gives at most g0+2<=3*g0 vertices. The interval belongs to one fixed carrier algebra and is never reset at carrier-sector changes.

At a planar tie, increasing versus decreasing coordinate order gives different residual greedy sets at every rank ell<G. Equality would make the common selected span contain both a covering prefix and suffix, hence the whole rank-G block. Therefore each capped gain g0 charges at least g0/2 planar truncation transitions, with disjoint rank intervals for different cost levels at one direction. Every rank-j functional prefix is a downset inside V_j^2 and the planar matroid bound gives O(j*log(j+1)) transitions. Summing j<=n bounds the entire off-carrier vertex charge by O(n^2*log(n+1)), independently of the number of carrier sectors.

A positive fan vertex on a carrier plane corresponds to a two-dimensional exposed basis-profile face. Projection along the one-dimensional plane kernel cannot collapse it to a point, so it is visible as a planar transition. The existing rational-shadow theorem charges O(n*log(n+1)*||q||_1^(1/3)) per plane. Isolated boundary-subdivision vertices are similarly visible in coordinate shadows; a collapsed supporting edge makes a coincident boundary wall, not an isolated crossing. Planarity then bounds the total cell count by the interior and boundary vertex counts, without assuming bounded vertex degree.

For the degree-r scaled-curve carrier, the r-1 wall normals are primitive versions of (r-h,0,-h), each with norm at most r. If r<sqrt(n), their total charge is O(n*r^(4/3)*log(n+1))<=O(n^(5/3)*log(n+1)), below the shared threshold budget. If r^2>=n, the previously proved surface-fan equality already gives O(n^2*log(n+1)). Thus the same absolute quadratic-power upper bound holds for every balanced generic component count, over all characteristics with suitable infinite-field generic samples. This supersedes the weaker family bound and closes its entire balanced polynomial-amplification route.

The general unequal-size formula min_s(n-A_s+d_s) can have additional active constraints and does not in general truncate a single carrier prefix. The finite error is |a-c/2|*r+E(C)+(c-K)_+/8. The last term is the exact nearest-integer quadratic loss; no floating fit supplies the proof.

At tau0=(c+K)/(2*gamma), c>K gives a rank deficit (c-K)*r^2/8+O(r), a limiting fraction (c-K)/(4*c) of n. The minimum possible K is four, so c>4 is necessary and sufficient for such a leading defect on an open fixed-weight region. The upper hook step is D(w)=2+ceil(w_y/w_x)+ceil(w_y/w_z)+ceil(min(w_x,w_z)/w_y), including zero hooks. A block of width h is h column progressions and 2h row progressions in the merged-axis/Y grid. Its rank B or B-1 threshold is bounded by using B points in its first column, giving all critical indices Q=O_(H,R)(L) on bounded aspect, and Q=O_(H,u,v)(L) on a bounded harmonic-ratio window. Axis rounding forces |mu*ell-nu*k|<=k+ell at a meeting of two template curves, with mu=N-i and nu=N'-i'. Only O(mu+nu) integer denominator pairs survive; their affine-piece events total O(L^4). On compact aspects, a line steeper than 2Q/k meets a curve at most once. For the other pairs, a*k=O(Q), and the number of small-coefficient lines is O((Q/k)^2+Q/k+1). Summing the latter piece budgets proves O_(H,R)(L^4), including coincident pieces, verticals and aspect boundaries.

For the all-aspect count put rho=w_x/w_z, h=rho/(1+rho), x=log(rho), U_i=v_i/h. The normalized axis statistic lies in [i,i+1] and has logarithmic derivative at most i+1 in magnitude. If a*c*k^2>d^2*(Q+1)^2, their difference is strictly monotone globally, giving one meeting. The remaining positive coefficient pairs satisfy a*c=O((Q/k)^2), so elementary divisor counting bounds them by O((Q/k)^2*log(Q+1)). Summing k^-2 gives O(L^4*log(L+1)). uniform_proofs: For bounded irregular profiles m_s=4(r-s)+e_s, |e_s|<=D, the exact tail differs from 2(r-s)^2 by at most (D+2)(r-s). At an extra capacity maximum the nonempty-hook increment error interval has width 2D+3+1/sigma, giving (K-4)*(s+1)<2*(2D+3+1/sigma). With R_D=64(D+2), T_D=4096(D+1), M_D=10^6(D+1)^2, every final surface prefix is a basis for r>=R_D if sigma<T_D^-1, sigma>T_D, or K*r^2>(2r+M_D)^2. The central proof splits at 2r/(sqrt(K)+2), using summed hook lower bounds and translated outside-grid area; tail positivity handles small remaining capacities. Thus every non-surface witness lies in (sigma-1)^2/sigma<=4M_D/r+M_D^2/r^2.

Normalize h=1 and 1/2<=sigma<=2. Taking m_s column points in each layer fits every quota and has cost at most B_D*r, B_D=2D+11; the full prefix therefore has actual rank n. Unit-cell bounds and the same endpoint optimization as the slope-four rank law give |R(C)-min(2r^2,C^2/(2sigma))|<=(D+2)r+6C+9. Integrating the exact greedy identity F(w)=integral(n-R(C))dC yields |F(w(p,sigma))-(8/3)r^3*sqrt(sigma)|<=E_D*r^2, E_D=2(D+2)B_D+3B_D^2+9B_D. Both estimates are uniform in p, including extreme aspects, and use actual positive-prefix ranks rather than an arbitrary residue-matroid equivalence.

The actual residue-basis profiles are integer points; a strict positive initial at nearby distinct monomial prices has a unique minimum basis and a distinct exposed profile vertex. At axis center p0 use dual coordinates V=(p0*w_x,w_y,(1-p0)*w_z), S_prime=(X/p0,Y,Z/(1-p0)), and chart V_z=1. The comparator is (8/3)r^3*sqrt(V_y*V_x*V_z/((1-p0)*V_x+p0*V_z)), with uniform slice Hessian norm <=1000r^3. On 4/5<=V_x,V_y<=6/5 its support error is <=2E_D*r^2.

Classical finite differences for concave support functions give tangential widths L=2H*epsilon+2e/epsilon and center-normal width N=e+H*epsilon^2+2epsilon*L. With epsilon=C_D/sqrt(r), these are O_D(r^(5/2)) and O_D(r^2). The actual integer-profile cap volume is 8*p0*(1-p0)*L^2*N=O_D(p0*(1-p0)*r^7), retaining the determinant of the nonunimodular rescaling. Applying the classical full-dimensional Andrews estimate yields O_D(sqrt(p0*(1-p0))*r^(7/2)) vertices per patch.

Degenerate cap hulls are treated in their own lattice: a planar cap has area O_D(r^5), induced lattice covolume at least one and O_D(r^(5/3)) vertices; dimensions zero/one have at most two. The actual full-rank cutoff forces x absent if p<1/(B_D*r), or z absent at the reflected end, giving elimination algebras of length n and O(n log(n+1)) planar initials. For the remaining p each dyadic interval has O_D(sqrt(r)) relative patches. Their vertex budgets sum geometrically with weight sqrt(p0), giving O_D(r^4)=O_D(n^2), with no unproved aspect-uniform Euclidean condition number.

Ordinary surface prefixes already number O(n^2 log(n+1)) by the classical convex-position screening argument. Adding the cap and planar-end budgets proves the complete bound for every bounded irregular perturbation, uniformly in the generic sampling construction and characteristic. Long blocks, changing partitions and Theta(sqrt(n)) final rank defects are included. uniform_proofs: For irrational p, complementary merged-axis costs are U_j=j+epsilon_p({j*p}), with epsilon_p(t)=min(t/(1-p),(1-t)/p). Direct hook counting decomposes eta_j into two sawtooths of frequencies p*sigma and (1-p)*sigma and a torus function of ({j*p},{j/sigma}). The torus function G={theta-u-epsilon_p(t)/sigma}+epsilon_p(t)/sigma has exact mean 1/2+1/(2*sigma), so centered hook error is eta+gamma/2. Its level sets split into O_c(1) convex polygon pieces, uniformly even at extreme aspects. This bounds interval sums by two circle discrepancies plus B_c=2*(c+2)*(c+3) times convex-set torus discrepancy, without assuming a false generic bounded-variation or Sturmian estimate.

For a nonempty canonical block, exact cumulative quota surplus is P_l=-delta*l*(h-l)/2 + sum_first_l(eta)-(l/h)*sum_block(eta). Nonnegativity implies delta*(h^2-1)/8<=E(floor(h/2))+E(h). Proximity permits at most two empty terminal hooks; trimming them adds at most 2*(c+3). This supplies a complete finite curvature/discrepancy inequality uniform in the last component size.

A fixed-grid bracketing argument and finite trigonometric approximation show that positive normalized rotation discrepancy forces one bounded integer frequency within O(1/h) of an integer. Starting phase changes only a unit complex factor; geometric sums supply the required frequency bound. The quota inequality and delta*h>=epsilon force this discrepancy at a comparable interval length.

The pointwise block bound makes sigma O_c(1/h) from a simple critical root sigma0. Forced frequencies then put p near m/(k*sigma0), 1-m/(k*sigma0), or (m-v/sigma0)/u. A quadratic norm excludes u=0 for bounded frequencies at large h; clipping outside centers to endpoints preserves the distance bound. The resulting finite set lies in Q(sqrt(c*(c-4))) uniformly in a,r and block location.

If delta tends to zero and p tends to an aspect outside that quadratic field, delta times the maximum canonical block width tends to zero: a saturating subsequence would converge to a member of the finite resonance set for some fixed epsilon. This necessary resonance condition is not sufficient for long blocks and is not a uniform power-saving count.

A vertical-strip approximation converts convex discrepancy tau into rectangle discrepancy at least tau^2/100. Positive product Fejer kernels with Q=ceil(64/zeta^2), zeta=tau^2/100, bracket rectangles with controlled integral error; bounded Fourier coefficients and geometric sums make the resonance parameters explicit. With tau=epsilon/(128*(B_c+2)), field height is O_c(epsilon^-4), cardinality O_c(epsilon^-12), radius constant O_c(epsilon^-10), and the sufficient minimum width O_c(epsilon^-14). These are coarse proved asymptotic bounds, not useful small-scale numerical predictions.

For p0=sqrt(2)-1 and 2*c*(c-4) nonsquare, the critical quadratic field is disjoint from Q(sqrt(2)). The nonzero quartic algebraic-integer norm of q*p0-a-b*sigma0 yields |p0-(a+b*sigma0)/q|>=1/((c+4)^3*H^4). Combining height O(epsilon^-4) and radius O(epsilon^-10)/h gives h<=O(epsilon^-26), with epsilon=delta*h, hence h=O_c(delta^(-26/27)). The subthreshold h<h0 case gives the stronger exponent 14/15. continuations.title: Common-ray reduction and a uniform relative-margin route to the sharp upper scale
continuations.previous_evidence: Revalidated clean 97a7081, all 304 tracked hashes, original goal/criteria and 50 prior records. The last result counted a restricted saturation subset, so the next work returned to a general matroid mechanism and its strongest directly matching primary comparison.
continuations.progress_classification: Established the common-ray rank ceiling/traversal and its published tropical boundary, then formulated a concrete uniform quotient-cone margin question whose proved packing implication would close the upper power gap. An infinite abstract rank-n hyperbolic-n matroid family refutes a rank/lattice-only margin proof, while a symbolic hard-quotient witness and 98 saved actual cones support feasibility. The uniform hypothesis is unproved and the original endpoint is unchanged.
uniform_proofs: The entire minimum-basis family of a matroid depends only on ordered element cost levels. Strictly increasing log therefore preserves minimum bases, including ties. For c_e=alpha_e*q_type(e), the transformed objective is log(product_B alpha_e)+sum_i k_i(B)*log(q_i). With a fixed ray-count vector, coefficient-product minimizers do not depend on q. Two distinct strict bases, or distinct strictly exposed profiles, cannot share that vector. There are binomial(r+t-1,t-1) compositions; the bound is independent of the number of ground elements and is sharp for a uniform matroid on t coefficient lists 1,...,r.

The transformed minimum is the degree-r tropical polynomial min_k(beta_k+k dot u). A direct sum of arbitrary ray matroids uses the same polynomial ceiling at total rank, so common positive fans of their profile polytopes cannot multiply separate counts. Componentwise fixed anchors add only fixed-rank linear translations and do not change this conclusion.

A basis is optimal exactly when every feasible single exchange has nonnegative cost. For each ordered pair of distinct ray types only the least ratio alpha_f/alpha_e matters; same-type inequalities are constant. Thus a strict cone has at most t*(t-1) interior facets, and its logarithmic image is a difference-constraint polyhedron. Breadth-first facet traversal uses at most 1+t*(t-1)*binomial(r+t-1,t-1) support calls, plus explicit O(r*(m-r)) exchange tests per new basis. Rational original-price inequalities avoid numerical logarithms.

If all positive quotient standard sets lie on the coordinate axes and 1, contract the always-selected 1 in the actual residue matroid to obtain rank n-1 on d rays. The all-field bound is binomial(n+d-2,d-1). Relations x_i*x_j=a*x_i+b*x_j+c suffice: they reduce mixed products to strictly cheaper pure powers at every positive weight.

Rational partial-fraction coordinates t and 1/(t-a_i), evaluated at n distinct nonpole nodes, attain every composition allocation of n-1. Multiplying by the common pole denominator gives a nonzero polynomial of degree at most n-1, proving independence at all n nodes. Hence the axis-carrier ceiling is sharp, including radical rational point ideals. It explains, rather than enlarges, the earlier quadratic three-pole family.

For general monomial weights, log(a dot w)=log(sum_i a_i*exp(u_i)) is not affine in u. An existing length-six quotient over F_101 has strict bases {1,x,y,z,z^2,y*z} and {1,x,y,z,z^2,x*z}, both with pure-axis counts (1,1,2), but different profiles. Exact matrix determinants, direct greedy and all strict minimal-border comparisons revalidate the obstruction. No superquadratic lower bound is inferred.

Conditional packing theorem: if every actual three-variable initial cone has relative margin mu(C)>=kappa/n for one absolute kappa>0, erode each normal z to z-kappa*abs(z)/(2n). Reduced-basis comparison entries are at most n, so clearing denominators gives O(n^2) coefficients. Three independent primitive extreme rays provide an integer interior center of height O(n^4), hence logarithmic aspect O(log n). Relative slack gives a contained log-aspect square of radius kappa/(4n). Disjoint-square packing yields G_3(n)=O(n^2*log(n+1)^2). The implication is proved, but its uniform-margin premise is not.

The previous wholly interior hard-cone family, of length 2k+1 and necessary quadratic integer height, has witness (4k+1,4k,4k^2-2k). Its relative slacks are 1/(8k+1), 1/(4k-1), 1/(8k+3), all at least 1/(4n). Thus the known hard arithmetic certificates do not refute the proposed relative robustness scale.

For n=10*(M+5), four explicit binary parallel classes at distinct axis weights with coefficients near M, plus n-4 distinct axis coloops, form a representable rank-n matroid on V_n^3. A positive cell has x/y and x/z ratios in consecutive Farey intervals of width O(M^-2), giving logarithmic area O(n^-4) and relative margin O(n^-2). uniform_proofs: For every length-n quotient in two or three variables, reduced-basis exponent comparisons have coordinates at most n. Given any finite monomial downset D0, every linear subspace of the span of its maximal monomials T is an ideal in K[x]/J because all variables annihilate it. Identifying disjoint pairs of these socle monomials gives an actual cyclic commuting quotient, with a free lower core and one independent residue class per pair. Every strict choice of cheaper pair representatives is a downset and has an explicit reduced binomial/monomial basis.

The planar antichain x^(k+2), x^2*y^(k-1), y^(k+1), x^(k+1)*y has divisor downset size 5k+1. Two pair identifications give length 5k-1 and slack matrix [[k,1-k],[-k-1,k]], of determinant one and positive inverse. Exactly three positive sign regions occur. The narrow cone has exact relative margin 1/(k+sqrt(k^2-1))^2 and logarithmic width log(k^2/(k^2-1)), both Theta(k^-2).

The three-variable antichain consists of heads x^(k+2), y^k, z^(4k+3) and tails x^2*y^(k-1)*z, x^(k+1)*z, x*y*z^2. Its divisor downset has size 12k+5. Three terminal pair identifications give length 12k+2. The full hard-cone matrix [[k,1-k,-1],[-k-1,k,-1],[-1,-1,4k+1]] has determinant one and an explicitly positive polynomial inverse. All seven sign patterns except the all-negative one occur, so the entire positive fan has seven initials over every field.

The integer witness (8k^2-2,8k^2+8k+2,4k+1) has unit slacks, giving margin at least 1/(16k^3+16k^2+4k-1). The positive dual row (2k+1,2k-1,1) maps the slack matrix to (0,0,1), bounding every witness margin above by 1/(16k^3+4k+1). In particular the actual length-50 case k=4 has margin below 1/1041, smaller than the former diagnostic threshold 1/800.

In the chart w_z=1, determinant one gives raw cone area 1/(2*(4k^2-1)). Its inverse columns satisfy w_x>=2k-1, w_y>=2k+1, w_x+w_y<=4k+1. The logarithmic Jacobian gives area between 2/((4k^2-1)*(4k+1)^2) and 1/(2*(4k^2-1)^2), hence Theta(n^-4). Every ideal supported at the origin has a canonical finite monomial parent formed from all monomials it contains. The coordinate annihilator depths of its nonzero relation module are at most n. uniform_result.general_matroid_bound: With rank r, hyperbolic budget H, b=3*(d-1)/((d+1)*(3*d-5)), A=C_d*(1+log(H+1))*(1+r+(r^2*H)^(1/3)), the basis-profile vertex count is O_d(A+A^b*(1+r*H)^((d-1)*(1-b))). No representability assumption.
uniform_result.quotient_bound: For every fixed d>=2 and field, G_d(n)<=O_d(n^e*(1+log(n+1))^b), e=2*d*(d-1)/(d+1)-(d-1)/((d+1)*(3*d-5)).

uniform_result.three_variable_count: The existing 23/8 power and 3/8 logarithm are reproduced, not improved.
uniform_result.higher_dimensions: For d>=5 retain the older, smaller Dey-based power. The new formula is not the best existing repository specialization in those dimensions.

equal_degree_unit_reduction.full_r2_integral_universal_basis: The finite union of the integral reduced bases contains a monic Groebner basis for every order and remains valid under arbitrary base change.
equal_degree_unit_reduction.full_r2_rank_query: O(s+1) exact arithmetic/floor operations and constant auxiliary storage for every positive weight.
equal_degree_unit_reduction.first_bad_prime_interaction_exponent: r=3 in the coefficient-one family: previous r=1 and current r=2 have none; previous fixed r=3 realizes every prime at some cutoff.

higher_seed_binomial_reduction.parameter_scope: r>a>=1, degree-a nonzero homogeneous binary Q,H; prices (u,u,Z), 0<u<Z; complete tiers
higher_seed_binomial_reduction.regular_pair_formula: For coprime Q,H, the exact rank is the homogeneous-channel sum of regular binomial blocks (B4)-(B5), independent of coefficients but retaining characteristic dependence.
higher_seed_binomial_reduction.noncoprime_bracket: Every nonzero pair lies between the canonical and regular sums (B3). The canonical lower bound is exact for Q=H=y^a.
higher_seed_binomial_reduction.original_integral_prefix_decomposition: For Q=x^2+y^2,H=xy, an integral homogeneous unit basis 1,x,y,x^2 splits the actual original seed into G_s, two G_(s-1) and G_(s-2), including ambient free modules.
higher_seed_binomial_reduction.exact_block_query: At rational prices, O_a(s^3*(1+s/r)^2) field operations, O_a(s^2) additional rational arithmetic/floor operations and O_a((1+s/r)^2) field elements of scratch; binomial generation and bit costs separate.
higher_seed_binomial_reduction.remaining_identity: Resolved: (B8) holds uniformly, with the stronger integral whole-prefix cokernel isomorphism proved in docs/higher_seed_transport.md.
higher_seed_binomial_reduction.equivalence: The core identity is equivalent to uniform regular/canonical seed equality, via triangular inversion of the degree-channel convolution.
higher_seed_binomial_reduction.conditional_fan_consequence: At a=2 the identity is sufficient for full original largest-z signed transfer and a uniform O(n) whole-family bound.
all_field_scope_counterexamples: Original r=3,s=5 at weight (9,9,4), cutoff 20: regular rank 15, canonical rank 14, outside u<Z.
Weighted core s=15,a=2,r=3, selected 21-column downward staircase: regular rank 21, canonical rank 20; the staircase is not a coherent positive prefix.
higher_seed_binomial_reduction.possible_digit_proof_route: Superseded as a necessary proof task by the integral flag transport and global cancellation. Classical Lucas and carry structure remain relevant arithmetic context, not a required unproved step.

three_point_rank_reduction.integral_component_identity: For every interval-selected positive or negative binomial block, its cokernel is exactly one degree component of a binary Artinian ideal generated by products of x,y,x+y, by homogenization and a unit triangular interval basis change. The free rank and all nonunit Smith invariant factors are preserved; unit pivot counts can differ.
three_point_rank_reduction.coherent_identity_equivalence: The rank/Hilbert-function-sum equivalence remains valid; (B8) and (P4) are now proved by integral transport.
three_point_rank_reduction.integral_symmetry: Every simultaneous permutation of x,y,x+y in the generators preserves component cokernels through GL_2(Z), up to signs.
three_point_rank_reduction.coherent_arithmetic_example: At s=11,a=2,r=3,u=1,Z=7,T=14 the k=2 regular block has component (Z[x,y]/(x^4,y^3,x^2*y^2,2*x^3*y))_4 = Z/2. Its local torsion agrees with the degree-two component of (x^2,y^2,(x+y)^2), but their whole algebras differ.
three_point_rank_reduction.scope_limit: Homogenization, basis changes, Hilbert functions and three-form symmetries are classical tools. This is a supporting proof reduction and an exact coherent obstruction to support matching; it is not a new syzygy-gap theorem, a fan bound, a prime-distribution result or goal completion.
three_point_rank_reduction.resolution: docs/higher_seed_transport.md proves the formerly open identity by integral row changes, a flag recurrence and a global index bijection. No p-fractal application or one-triple syzygy-gap identification is required.

higher_seed_transport.parameter_scope: r>a>=1, all s>=0, complete cutoffs T, and prices 0<u<Z; integral coefficient-one cores, then all-field nonzero degree-a binary forms via the existing sandwich.
higher_seed_transport.integral_core_theorem: The complete regular and canonical core prefix cokernels are isomorphic as finitely generated abelian groups, preserving their free ranks and every nonunit Smith factor, hence all prime-power torsion. The original core matrices have the same shape and the same full Smith normal forms. Auxiliary presentations can have different unit counts.
higher_seed_transport.mechanism: Integral shifts put both block systems into the same negative-power axis flags. A unit-constant row quotient transports flag cokernels along (m,k)->(m+r,k+r-a). Each negative index contribution has the unique positive predecessor obtained by e=floor(k/r); unmatched positive contributions transport to zero flags. Cancellation is in the split direct-sum group of finitely generated abelian groups, not an exact-sequence Euler group that loses torsion.
higher_seed_transport.noncoprime_seed_consequence: The complete equal-binary-price rank is coefficient-independent for every pair of nonzero binary forms of degree a, retaining characteristic dependence.
higher_seed_transport.original_integral_seed_consequence: The integral four-core decomposition (B9) transfers the cokernel isomorphism to the original quadratic-pair and canonical seeds, including all prime-power torsion.
higher_seed_transport.full_original_signed_transfer: For every r>=2, all s, all fields and generic positive weights with y cheapest, the original standard set equals that for the signed face deleting y^2; exchange x,y for the other region.
higher_seed_transport.full_original_fan_bound: g(I_(s,r)) <= 25*n+14 uniformly in r>=2 and field, n=(s+1)^2. Two signed-graded regions contribute at most 12*n+7 each, and the exact cheapest-z count is at most n.
higher_seed_transport.same_degree_obstruction: s=17,a=2,r=3,u=9/17,Z=1,T=17/3,m=0: regular length-six block cokernel Z, canonical cokernel zero, over the integers.
higher_seed_transport.old_scope_counterexamples_preserved: The opposite price regime and arbitrary divisor-closed selections still have the exact earlier counterexamples. Coherence is used by the cutoff and the pairing.
higher_seed_transport.scope_limit: A uniform structural theorem and a full construction-family exclusion. It does not settle unrestricted G_3, establish a new prime-distribution or p-fractal result, certify exact priority, or meet the original impact/publication endpoint.

liaison_fan_composition.all_field_construction: For monic univariate f(x),g(y),h(z) of degrees a,b,c, (g,h) subset J1 and (f,h) subset J2, H=(h,fg)+f*J1+g*J2 has length abc+m1+m2.
liaison_fan_composition.prior_art_boundary: The algebraic operation and additive length are classical liaison addition, positively matched to Hartshorne--Migliore--Nagel Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2(a), not evidence of a new construction.
liaison_fan_composition.exact_initial_formula: For every global monomial order, in(H)=(z^c,x^a*y^b)+x^a*in(J1)+y^b*in(J2). Its positive fan is exactly the common refinement; only branch-cone pairs with nonempty open intersection occur.
liaison_fan_composition.uniform_box_prefix_refinement: Every active wall of an ordinary m-point positive box prefix has primitive direction product at most 2*m. Any finite common refinement with all m<=M therefore has O(M^2*log(M+1)^4) cells, independently of component count or box caps.
liaison_fan_composition.local_moment_comparison: g(H)=O((1+S1+S2)^(3/2)) for local branches at the origin, with Si their m-adic degree moments. The fixed box/tag profile is a translation, not a varying moment budget.
liaison_fan_composition.balanced_nonlinear_rectangle_gate: For J1=(y^q,z^q,x-F(y,z)) and J2=(x^q,z^q,y-G(x,z)), with arbitrary zero-constant F,G over any field, this gluing has N=q^3+2*q^2, S1=S2=q^2*(q-1), hence g(H)=O(N^(3/2)).
liaison_fan_composition.quantitative_decision: Preserve the exact composition tool but do not search larger generic box-prefix compositions or balanced local-rectangle glues for a power gain. They are uniformly excluded. Arbitrary dependent branches are not classified.
liaison_fan_composition.scope_limit: A classical operation, an all-order affine fan formula and two proof-based feasibility gates. They do not produce an amplified realizable family, change the unrestricted bound, or establish publication significance.
liaison_fan_composition.identical_branch_exact_witnesses: results/research/liaison_fan_checks.json: complete_identical_fan_fixtures contains every branch standard set and exact cone polygon.

two_interaction_rank_identity.hypotheses: Any field; nonzero homogeneous binary quadratics Q,H,L; odd r>=3; s=2*r+1; A=K[x,y,z]/(z^2+Q+H*z^r+L*z^(r+1), m^(s+1)).
two_interaction_rank_identity.exact_columns: At most one high substitution survives; (C3) gives all monomial columns integrally with no division by 2 or the power exponent.
two_interaction_rank_identity.selected_prefix: All a+b+2*c<=r+3, a complete price prefix rather than an arbitrary selected staircase.
two_interaction_rank_identity.rank: 2*r^2+6*r+13-delta; the coupled outside-reference domain has dimension r^2-r and kernel dimension delta.
two_interaction_rank_identity.r_3_criterion: delta=1 if and only if H divides Q*L.
two_interaction_rank_identity.odd_r_at_least_5_criterion: delta=1 if and only if H^2 divides Q*L^2.
two_interaction_rank_identity.uniform_comparison: Q=x^2+y^2,H=x*y,L=x^2 has delta=0; the same Q,H with L=x*y has delta=1. Changing only the second high form gives a rank gap of one over every field and every odd r>=3.
two_interaction_rank_identity.characteristic_control: Q=H=x^2+y^2,L=x^2+x*y: delta=1 over all fields for r=3, but for odd r>=5 exactly in characteristic two.
two_interaction_rank_identity.support_lattice: The independent-form equation has support-difference rank three and constant index four. This is not asserted to identify its intrinsic profile lattice.
two_interaction_rank_identity.fan_consequence: The two quotients have different realized standard sets at some generic nearby weights. No inequality between their total numbers of initial ideals follows.

power_carrier_bounds.pure_carrier_hypothesis: I contains a degree-m polynomial with all three pure degree-m coefficients nonzero; S bounds all initial-standard total degree moments.
power_carrier_bounds.all_field_bound: g(I)=O(min((S+1)*sqrt(b+1),(b+1)*(S+1)^(2/3))); b=min(S,(m-1)*n). Group by largest variable, then apply classical lattice-vertex bounds to bounded-coordinate profile hulls.
power_carrier_bounds.truncated_hypersurface: For fixed-degree homogeneous q with all pure coefficients nonzero and h starting at degree D>deg(q), I=(q+h,m^(s+1)) contains q^e for e=ceil((s+1)/D). Its length is Theta_a(s^2), so g(I)=O_a(sqrt(e)*n^2).
power_carrier_bounds.bounded_interaction_depth_decision: If D>=c*s for fixed c>0, g(I)=O_(a,c)(n^2), independently of the number or coefficients of higher terms and characteristic. Do not expand this family to seek a power gain.
power_carrier_bounds.necessary_growth_condition: A putative n^(2+epsilon) lower family within these pure-tangent hypersurfaces needs e=Omega(n^(2*epsilon)), hence D=O(n^(1/2-2*epsilon)) for fixed tangent degree.
power_carrier_bounds.two_interaction_application: q=x^2+y^2+z^2, s=2*r+1, D=r+2 gives q^2 in I and the uniform O(n^2) fan bound. Arbitrary Q missing a pure coefficient is outside this application.
power_carrier_bounds.generic_coordinate_corollary: Every length-n three-variable ideal has a nonzero relation of degree O(n^(1/3)). A nonempty open set of linear changes makes its three pure top coefficients nonzero, giving O(n^(8/3)) initials after such a change, over a finite extension if needed for a finite field.
power_carrier_bounds.generic_coordinate_scope_limit: No claim of invariance under linear changes, no bound on original-coordinate G_3, no arithmetic-operation bound, and no novelty certificate.
power_carrier_bounds.entry_wall_obstruction: At r=3 over Q, an actual wall X+Y=3*Z is absent from every coordinate normal-form entry list. An exact ideal multiplier, both full adjacent cones and their one-monomial exchange are saved.
power_carrier_bounds.classical_inputs: Andrews lattice-vertex exponents, the Babson--Onn--Thomas state dictionary, the existing relative-socle layer argument, and the already used elementary power identity.

oracle_fan_enumeration.input_scope: One marked reduced Groebner basis under a known global monomial order, or commuting coordinate-multiplication matrices with a cyclic vector. Arbitrary generators require additional initial-basis computation.
oracle_fan_enumeration.truncated_state: Q=(B(I)+R_+^3) intersect {sum<=n^2+1}; all state vertices lie below the cut; new vertices come only from coordinate-ray edges. Q is a full-dimensional integer polytope with at most 4*g vertices.
oracle_fan_enumeration.exact_vertex_oracle: Formulas (O7)--(O9) use lexicographic greedy keys, including zero and boundary directions. Symbolic negative coordinate perturbations and one extra tie term return a genuine polytope vertex and an actual initial-basis label in every characteristic.
oracle_fan_enumeration.support_queries: At most 12*g+1, including initialization, by attributed vertex/facet oracle reconstruction and three-dimensional Euler bounds.
oracle_fan_enumeration.field_operations: O((g+1)*n^3*(1+log(n+1))^2), including column preprocessing and all reduced-basis recovery.
oracle_fan_enumeration.geometric_operations: O((g+1)^2*log(g+2)+(g+1)*n*(1+log(n+1))^3), using the cited exact 3D hull routine with degeneracy handling.
oracle_fan_enumeration.unrestricted_shadow_consequence: O(n^(47/8)*(1+log(n+1))^(19/8)) field operations, with a lower-order rational-geometric budget.
oracle_fan_enumeration.classical_boundary: The reconstruction and greedy conversion are established. Classical g=O(n^3) plus these tools already gives O(n^6*L^2), distinct from the older direct-zonotope O(n^7*L^10). The shadow theorem supplies only the extra 1/8 exponent saving.
oracle_fan_enumeration.output_representation: All marked reduced bases and the state fan; their union is a universal basis, possibly represented with repeated polynomials. No minimum-size or canonical duplicate-free output claim.
oracle_fan_enumeration.verification_implementation_limit: The bounded checker enumerates hull triples and all tiny determinant bases; it is not the asymptotically efficient hull implementation or a production benchmark.

multiplicative_shadow_obstruction.realization: Six incomparable socle monomials from the positive diagonal and negative off-diagonal rows of N(t), with three independent pair identifications, define an actual cyclic quotient over every field.
multiplicative_shadow_obstruction.strict_visibility: q^perp meets the cone interior if and only if p=q*N(t)^(-1) has both positive and negative entries. Merely touching a wall is insufficient.
multiplicative_shadow_obstruction.minimum_primitive_plane_product: Theta(t^8)=Theta(n(t)^(4/3)); product is the product of abs(q_i)+1.
multiplicative_shadow_obstruction.proof_mechanism: Unimodular integral pullback, mixed-sign norm expansion through three factors, a small row-sum budget forcing two large coordinates, and positive common orthogonals preventing simultaneous cancellation of two leading coefficients.
multiplicative_shadow_obstruction.explicit_upper_witness: q=(1,-1,0)*N(t), primitive by unimodularity; N(t)^(-1)*(1,1,1)^T is a strictly positive witness on its plane.
multiplicative_shadow_obstruction.refuted_shortcut: A uniform O(n) primitive product plane detecting each positive initial cone.
multiplicative_shadow_obstruction.scope_limit: A uniform feasibility obstruction with only seven initials. It directs the main argument toward collective counting; it neither improves the unrestricted count nor meets the impact/publication endpoint.

rational_plane_transfer.general_transfer: For a full-dimensional lattice P in R^d, rational-plane shadows bounded by A*(1+height^theta) give f0(P)<=C*(A*h^((d-2)*(d+theta)/(d-1))+surface(P)/h).
rational_plane_transfer.classical_lattice_inputs: A primitive integer objective w lies in a rational plane of covolume O_d(norm(w)^((d-2)/(d-1))); O_d(T^d) such planes have height at most T. Both are classical, with proofs supplied.
rational_plane_transfer.short_plane_sharpness: For w=(1,t,...,t^(d-1)), the exact minimum primitive Plucker infinity height among containing planes is t^(d-2). The height exponent is therefore optimal; no novelty is asserted for this elementary observation.
rational_plane_transfer.general_matroid_bound: With rank r, hyperbolic budget H, b=3*(d-1)/((d+1)*(3*d-5)), A=C_d*(1+log(H+1))*(1+r+(r^2*H)^(1/3)), the basis-profile vertex count is O_d(A+A^b*(1+r*H)^((d-1)*(1-b))). No representability assumption.
rational_plane_transfer.quotient_bound: For every fixed d>=2 and field, G_d(n)<=O_d(n^e*(1+log(n+1))^b), e=2*d*(d-1)/(d+1)-(d-1)/((d+1)*(3*d-5)).
rational_plane_transfer.four_variable_improvement: G_4(n)=O(n^(33/7)*log(n+1)^(9/35)); power gain 1/77 over the older repository 52/11 bound.
rational_plane_transfer.three_variable_count: The existing 23/8 power and 3/8 logarithm are reproduced, not improved.
rational_plane_transfer.higher_dimensions: For d>=5 retain the older, smaller Dey-based power. The new formula is not the best existing repository specialization in those dimensions.
rational_plane_transfer.three_variable_transfer_budget: Substitution of A=O(n*polylog(n)) and theta>=0 in the same transfer and quartic surface budget gives power 4-6/(5+theta), at best 14/5. This is only a limit of that substitution, not an actual-count lower bound or a proof of the hypothetical height-independent shadow envelope.
rational_plane_transfer.scope_limit: A general geometric/matroid theorem and a higher-dimensional refinement. The original three-variable sharp-growth or separating-family target remains unchanged and unresolved.

cyclic_interleaving_fans.quotient: A=B tensor K[g]/(g^m-1), x=U*g,y=V*g,z=g, length n=m*r. For generic B=K^r take algebraically independent point coordinates over a function-field extension of any base field.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.characteristic_scope: Works in every characteristic, including characteristic dividing m. The all-monomial uniform rank claim is over the function-field model; finite specializations only assert the finitely many ranks controlling the entire positive fan.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.exact_rank: For any finite S, sum over colors j of min(r, number of distinct (a,b) with a+b+c=j modulo m). Reduce c modulo m and count duplicate columns once.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.general_tensor_converse: Every finite Z/m-graded quotient with all variables of degree one and z^m=1 has this form with arbitrary planar B=A_0. In the general case the stream rank is the actual planar column rank, not the generic minimum.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.collective_facet_charge: At fixed primitive planar direction (p,q), a profile facet with vertical width l has at most 4*l vertices. All positive facets at that direction have total vertical jump at most n*(m-1).
cyclic_interleaving_fans.fixed_period_count: O_m(n^2*log(n+1)), using pq<=32*m^2*n+256*m^4 and the existing boundary-cell bound.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.shared_ground: With K0=ceil((r-1)/m), all sector selections use one ground of size O(r*log(r+1)*(K0+1+log(r+1))). Ordering that ground fixes every stream without a factor for the number of colors.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.comparable_period_count: For every fixed c>0 and m>=c*r, O_c(n^2*log(n+1)^8).
cyclic_interleaving_fans.exact_stabilization: For r>=2 and m>=r, g(I_(r,m))=g(I_(r,r)). Within each cheapest-variable sector the linear cost map preserves all selection grounds; cheapest ties are actual walls. Standard monomial labels and quotient lengths are not unchanged.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.coarse_general_bound: O(n^(5/2)), uniformly for arbitrary planar B in the tensor converse. This is a classical normalized-volume consequence of the index-m grading and z^m relation.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.necessary_polynomial_window: A generic family with g>=c*n^(2+epsilon) needs m>=Omega(n^(epsilon/3)*L^(-1/3)) and m<=O(n^(1/2-epsilon/12)*L^(2/3)). These are necessary conditions only.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.nongeneric_scope_obstruction: B=F7^3 with U=V=(1,2,4), m=2: x,y have actual rank one while the generic minimum rule predicts two. The sharper gates and stabilization are not asserted for arbitrary B.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.edge_route: The proved inequality T_(1/2)<=2*L_+ connects square-root normal incidence to positive-facet edge length. The unrestricted cubic budget remains unproved; its n^(33/13) consequence is conditional.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.scope_limit: An exact realizable interleaving model, generic-family counting gates and a concrete surviving parameter regime. These do not settle the unrestricted target or establish publication significance.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.all_parameter_generic_count: g(I_(r,m))=O(n^2*log(n+1)^2), n=m*r, with an absolute constant for every r,m.
cyclic_interleaving_fans.remaining_generic_window: None: the threshold dichotomy now closes all generic period/rank regimes.

cyclic_interleaving_uniform_count.uniform_count: g(I_(r,m))=O(n^2*log(n+1)^2), n=m*r, with an absolute constant for every r,m.
cyclic_interleaving_uniform_count.scope: Generic planar evaluation columns over the function-field extension of any base field, including characteristic dividing the period. The broader strong-grading converse with arbitrary planar B does not inherit the uniform-minimum rank rule or this count.
cyclic_interleaving_uniform_count.threshold_synchronization: After subtracting j times the cheapest weight, the r-th core thresholds tau_j are nonincreasing, with tau_0<=tau_(m-1)+alpha, alpha=m*w_min.
cyclic_interleaving_uniform_count.large_threshold_lemma: For tau_0>=2*alpha the union of all selected monomials has axis-box volume <=2048*n. Explicit strictly cheaper color-zero integer rectangles prove the bound, including when coordinate maxima occur in different colors.
cyclic_interleaving_uniform_count.dyadic_count: Pad rounded axis sides to one fixed dyadic product O(n); there are O(log(n+1)^2) boxes. Each retained integer-profile hull, regularized by a unit cube, has volume O(n^4), so the established Andrews vertex theorem gives O(n^2) vertices per box.
cyclic_interleaving_uniform_count.small_threshold_lemma: For tau_0<2*alpha all selected cores have k=0 or 1 and b+c<2*m. Core moments are integer affine coordinates for the original profile. Their regularized volume is O(n^3*m^2), hence O(n^4) when m<=r. For m>r use the earlier exact period stabilization at length r^2<=n.
cyclic_interleaving_uniform_count.full_family_decision: The former intermediate generic regime is closed. No r,m scaling in this family gives polynomial amplification above the ordinary three-variable corner-cut scale.
cyclic_interleaving_uniform_count.unconditional_box_obstruction: For every s>=3, m=s^3,r=s^4 and weights (L,L+1,L+2*m), L=8*m^3, give strict actual bases containing x^m,y^(m-1),z^(s^2). The axis-box volume/length is >s. Both m and r/m grow; these lie in the two-layer branch.
cyclic_interleaving_uniform_count.exact_full_basis_selection: Accessible-lattice min-heaps pop exactly r times in each color, using O(n*log(r+1)) exact arithmetic/comparison operations and O(r) queue/seen working storage plus O(n) if retaining output. This uses standard best-first enumeration; no bit-complexity, new general heap technique or smooth-number random-access claim.
cyclic_interleaving_uniform_count.classical_inputs: Andrews lattice-vertex theorem and the existing state-profile dictionary; source scopes and the established grading framework remain recorded. No new lattice-vertex exponent or completed priority assessment.

cyclotomic_overlap.scope: Finite monic algebra towers A=F[T]/g, F=K[x]/f, deg f=D, deg_T g=R, generators X=x,Y=u*T,Z=v*T with u,v units; n=D*R. All fields, arbitrary positive weights, no reducedness assumption.
cyclotomic_overlap.exact_low_background: Restrict to a<D,b+c<R. Its minimum basis C_rho is the direct sum of D-column slot bases, rho=(gamma-beta)/alpha, without a layer-separation hypothesis.
cyclotomic_overlap.exact_full_basis_reduction: B=(C_rho minus Q) union H, H the selected columns of tag degree >=R, |Q|=|H|. Minimum-basis sensitivity rejects all previously rejected low columns even after high columns are added.
cyclotomic_overlap.degree_excess: For sorted tag degrees d_i, d_i>=floor(i/D). With J0=n*(R-1)/2 and E=sum d_i-J0, E>=0.
cyclotomic_overlap.high_column_count: If M=|H|=D*q+s, 0<=s<D, then E>=D*q*(q+1)/2+s*(q+1)>=M^2/(2*D), hence M^2<=D*n*(D-1)*alpha/min(beta,gamma).
cyclotomic_overlap.nilpotent_tag_corollary: When g(T)=T^R, the whole positive fan at all prices has at most 2*(D-1)*(R-1)+2<2*n initials for D,R>=2. Degenerate one-dimensional cases have at most two.
cyclotomic_overlap.coherent_integrality_in_cheap_regions: For the pairwise-coprime three-circuit construction, all bases in the three earlier cheap-coordinate regions have integer index one, using the established two-circuit unimodularity theorem blockwise. Regional initials agree over all characteristics.
cyclotomic_overlap.general_arithmetic_boundary: In a finite integral algebra free over Z, a strict rational standard basis with determinant d persists modulo p exactly when p does not divide d. This is an elementary finite-column form of the established lucky-prime/base-change principle, not a new general modular theorem.
cyclotomic_overlap.coherent_arithmetic_witness: Equal periods (3,3,3), length 8, at weight (269002,209961,210033): standard set {1,X,X^2,Y,Y^2,Z,Z^2,YZ} has index 2 and rank 7 modulo 2. Exact exhaustive cones give 9 rational initials (6 index-one, 3 index-two), 6 in characteristic 2 and the rational fan in every odd characteristic.
cyclotomic_overlap.uniform_power_lift: For every odd k, S_3(U^k),S_3(V^k),S_3(W^k) with pair-product generators gives I_k=I_1(X^k,Y^k,Z^k), length 8*k^3, the same positive fan, and coherent cokernel (Z/2)^(k^3) on three cones. Index 2^(k^3) grows while fan counts stay 9 or 6; substituted coefficients do not grow.
cyclotomic_overlap.scope_limit: The coherent defect has repeated periods. No characteristic change, full fan count or amplification for three distinct coprime prime periods is proved. Neither abstract nonregularity nor coherent determinant size establishes many orderings.
cyclotomic_overlap.completed_layer_count: For every integer K>=1, all weights min(beta,gamma)>(D-1)*alpha/(K+1) together give O(n^(3/2)*sqrt(D)*K) initials, with an absolute constant. Integer coordinates (mu_x,mu_exp,E) have unit-regularized profile volume <=64*n^3*D*K^2. Apply the established Andrews vertex theorem once to the entire region, in each of two tag orders.
cyclotomic_overlap.comparable_period_all_price_count: If max(r,s,t)/min(r,s,t)<=C_p, then g(A)=O_(C_p)(n^(7/3)) in all characteristics, including nonreduced cases, across all positive prices.
cyclotomic_overlap.current_scope_limit: No sharp family count, superquadratic actual lower family, unrestricted G3 improvement or publication significance is established. The repeated-period arithmetic controls from the preceding turn are preserved but do not classify the distinct-prime field case.

cyclotomic_completed_bands.tower_scope: A=F[T]/g, F=K[x]/f, deg f=D, deg_T g=R, n=D*R; generators X=x,Y=u*T,Z=v*T with u,v units. Both defining polynomials monic. Every field, arbitrary coefficients, including nonreduced algebras.
cyclotomic_completed_bands.completed_layer_theorem: Let kappa=floor((D-1)*alpha/min(beta,gamma)). Every low-basis layer j<R-kappa remains in the full optimum. Thus at most D*min(kappa,R) high-tag columns enter.
cyclotomic_completed_bands.fixed_residual_rank: If kappa<=K, contract the fixed span F+F*T+...+F*T^(max(0,R-K)-1). Its quotient column matroid has rank D*min(K,R), and only selected tag degrees <=R-1+K remain. This is a vector-space contraction, generally not an algebra quotient. In the explicit tower coordinates it deletes the completed tag rows.
cyclotomic_completed_bands.quadratic_excess: For 1<=K<=R, E=mu_tag-n*(R-1)/2 lies in [0,D*K*(3*K-1)/2]. For K>=R use E<=n*(R-1)/2+n*K. The completed prefix fixes its whole tag moment, rather than paying the earlier O(n*K) budget in the small-band regime.
cyclotomic_completed_bands.uniform_region_count: For every integer K>=1, all weights min(beta,gamma)>(D-1)*alpha/(K+1) together give O(n^(3/2)*sqrt(D)*K) initials, with an absolute constant. Integer coordinates (mu_x,mu_exp,E) have unit-regularized profile volume <=64*n^3*D*K^2. Apply the established Andrews vertex theorem once to the entire region, in each of two tag orders.
cyclotomic_completed_bands.quadratic_region: K=O(sqrt(R)) gives O(n^2). In comparable coprime circuit periods of size q this broadens the cheap-axis quadratic exclusion from tag prices of order q^2*alpha to order q^(3/2)*alpha.
cyclotomic_completed_bands.intermediate_region_count: For comparable periods and tag prices at least c*q*alpha, K=O_c(R) gives O_c(n^2*sqrt(R))=O_c(n^(13/6)). No matching lower bound or exclusion of every smaller polynomial gain follows.
cyclotomic_completed_bands.periodic_carrier: For pairwise-coprime periods r,s,t, put M=3*(r+s+t)+1. The earlier bounded periodic representatives produce three binomials X_i^M-X^a_i with |a_i|<M. Their sum is an actual ideal member with pure top coefficients one over every field.
cyclotomic_completed_bands.all_price_parameter_bound: With D_1=(r-1)*(s-1), D_2=(r-1)*(t-1), D_3=(s-1)*(t-1), all positive prices obey g(A)<=C*n^(3/2)*sum_i sqrt(min(D_i,M)*product_(j!=i)D_j). Group by largest-price variable and use the established profile/volume dictionary.
cyclotomic_completed_bands.comparable_period_all_price_bound: If max(r,s,t)/min(r,s,t)<=C_p, then g(A)=O_(C_p)(n^(7/3)) in all characteristics, including nonreduced cases, across all positive prices.
cyclotomic_completed_bands.classical_boundary: The all-price periodic exponent is a direct classical lattice-volume consequence of the preceding bounded-representative and pure-axis-degree lemmas. It is not a new lattice-vertex theorem. Completed-layer retention is the changed structural input in the regional count; its exact priority is not certified.
cyclotomic_completed_bands.scope_limit: No sharp family count, superquadratic actual lower family, unrestricted G3 improvement or publication significance is established. The repeated-period arithmetic controls from the preceding turn are preserved but do not classify the distinct-prime field case.
